title: Microsoft 365 Apps admin center: Update Repair in Inventory
summary: The briefing's rollout information, repair prerequisites, control paths and command match the supplied records and Microsoft documentation. It correctly distinguishes the roadmap's launched status from Learn's preview wording and leaves the undocumented default and feature-specific licensing unresolved.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Update Repair identifies Windows devices with outdated Microsoft 365 Apps or update problems in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
claims.quote: Update Repair in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center helps you find Windows devices with Microsoft 365 Apps that are out of date or reporting update problems.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Admins can remotely start Online Repair for eligible devices.
claims.quote: admins can review device status and recommended actions, remotely start Online Repair for eligible devices, and follow manual remediation guidance for devices that need attention.

claims.claim: Update Repair uses Inventory data including installed version and build, target version policy and Click-to-Run errors.
claims.quote: Update Repair uses device data reported to Inventory, including the installed Microsoft 365 Apps version and build, the target version policy, and Click-to-Run error information.

claims.claim: The report compares the installed version with the latest version for the configured update channel.
claims.quote: It compares the installed version with the latest version available for the device's configured update channel and assigns a status.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Devices; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Only Needs repair and Needs attention devices appear in Update Repair.
claims.quote: The report shows devices in the Needs repair and Needs attention states. Devices that are Up to date or Outdated aren't shown because they don't currently require remediation.

claims.claim: A device at least one version behind with an error needing no separate remediation qualifies as Needs repair.
claims.quote: The device is at least one version behind and has an error that doesn't require separate remediation

claims.claim: A device at least three versions behind with no reported error qualifies as Needs repair.
claims.quote: or it's at least three versions behind and has no reported error.

claims.claim: Needs attention includes devices with errors requiring separate remediation.
claims.quote: The device has an error that requires separate remediation

claims.claim: Devices otherwise qualifying for repair but running builds earlier than 16.0.20326.20000 are Needs attention.
claims.quote: or it otherwise qualifies for repair but is running a Microsoft 365 Apps build earlier than 16.0.20326.20000.

claims.claim: The remote Repair action is unavailable for Needs attention devices.
claims.quote: Devices in the Needs attention state can't be repaired by the Repair action.

claims.claim: Update Repair requires Windows devices with Microsoft 365 Apps installed.
claims.quote: The device runs Windows and has Microsoft 365 Apps installed.

claims.claim: Devices must appear in Inventory and report current data.
claims.quote: The device appears in Inventory and reports current data.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope: Repair eligibility; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Repair action requires Microsoft 365 Apps build 16.0.20326.20000 or later.
claims.quote: To be eligible for the Repair action, the device must run Microsoft 365 Apps build 16.0.20326.20000 or later.

claims.claim: Repair triggers Click-to-Run Online Repair.
claims.quote: The action triggers Click-to-Run Online Repair.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Repair closes open Microsoft 365 Apps.
claims.quote: Repair interrupts users and closes open Microsoft 365 Apps.

claims.quote: Repair reinstalls Microsoft 365 Apps using the latest available build for the device’s configured update channel.
